messages.subject: Exon array analysis with FIRMA
parts:
Hi, I am trying out FIRMA for an exon array analysis project. I
followed the example in the vignette, and it worked brilliantly :-)

However, I need some clarifications on the FIRMA scores. Is it correct
that I need to apply log2 to the matrix obtained from
extractDataFrame*(fs) to obtain the actual FRIMA score? Like this:

#FIRMA
firma <- FirmaModel(plmTr)
fit(firma, verbose=verbose)
fs <- getFirmaScores(firma)

#extract firma score
fsScores<-log2(extractDataFrame(fs)) # Is this right?

Secondly, according to the Bioinformatics paper, FIRMA score is the
scaled median residuals of the fitted RMA model per probe. According
to the paper, residuals are calculated by

rijk = yijk - ci - pk
= (observed probe intensity) - (expected probe intensity based on
the fitted model)

Does it mean that it is a large negative FIRMA score that would
indicate exon skipping? This is because in those cases the observed
probe intensity should be smaller than the expected intensity obtained
from the RMA model.

Thanks in advance.

Joshua

messages.author: 1ff63ac4948de366
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Exon array analysis with FIRMA
parts:
Hi Joshua.

Correct on both accounts. You will need to take log2 of the extracted
FIRMA scores ... and a large negative FIRMA score may be indicative of
exon skipping. But, be careful since negative residuals can occur for
other reasons as well.

Its quite useful to plot the probe-level data (or the FIRMA scores)
relative to the known genomic annotation.

Cheers,
Mark

messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Re: Exon array analysis with FIRMA
parts:
> Its quite useful to plot the probe-level data (or the FIRMA scores)
> relative to the known genomic annotation.

Sorry, I guess what I really mean here is if you do identify a
probeset with a strong negative FIRMA score, it is generally always
useful to plot the probe-level data for the entire gene for all your
samples. Sometimes you can identify what known isoforms are being
expressed (if the isoforms are known). There are some striking
examples in the supplementary material of the Bfx paper.

Cheers,
Mark

Now this is another question. I would like to do some sort of probe
selection prior to running FIRMA. Currently I do filtering after
obtaining the FIRMA scores, but I wonder if I will get better results
if I do probe selection before model fitting. The intuition is that
removing non-responsive probes/probesets prior to fitting the RMA
model should reduce the overall noise and therefore increase the
discovery rate. If this is true, how can I specify that in
aroma.affymetrix?

Also, I wonder how did you draw those gene model diagrams in the
supplementary figures of your paper? Did you use any publicly
available packages? or did you write your own script to do so?

Many thanks.

Joshua

messages.author: 43e2e19dd6bd2992
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] Re: Exon array analysis with FIRMA
parts:
Hi Joshua,

We don't currently have implementation for filtering the probes before
fitting the RMA model. It is something I would like to do, but haven't
gotten around to. The only way to do it currently, I believe, is to make
a new cdf that contains only those probes, but this is not a fun process
and subject to a lot of errors.

In terms of the plots, I relied on the GenomeGraphs package, but I have
made a lot of additions to the exon array drawing functions; they are
going to be contributed to the package, but they are not yet released.
However, there is probably enough functionality as it is in GenomeGraphs
to do what you want (look at help('ExonArray-class') after you've loaded
the package to see a basic example).

I also have a wrapper function that seamlessly calls all of these lower
level functions and which created those pictures (basically saves a lot
of work on the part of the user). But again, it relies on waiting on
those contributed functions to be included in GenomeGraphs. When that is
all put together, I will make an announcement on this group page and
perhaps post example code on the ExonArray vignette page. I'm thinking
this should happen in the next few weeks, but as I'm not a maintainer of
the package I don't have a lot of control over the timing.

Best,
Elizabeth
